```{r setup, include=FALSE}
# Available on CRAN
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(magrittr)
library(tibble)
library(janitor)
library(tidyr)

# Available on Bioconductor
library(NanoTube)
```

# Resources 
https://nanostring.com/wp-content/uploads/MAN-C0019-08_nSolver_4.0_Analysis_Software_User_Manual.pdf


```{r}
sample_metadata_filepath <- "/root/capsule/data/tak188-mouse-preclinical-nanostring-v2/"
rcc_filepath <- "/root/capsule/data/tak188-mouse-preclinical-nanostring-v2"
```

# Read in data

```{r}
sample_info <- read.csv(file.path(sample_metadata_filepath, "20260408_metadata.csv"))
# Add a 'replicate' column to sample_info
sample_info %<>%
   group_by(treatment, day) %>%
   mutate(replicate = row_number()) %>%
   ungroup()

# List all files with .RCC extension in the specified directory
rcc_files <- list.files(rcc_filepath, 
                  pattern = "\\.RCC$", 
                  full.names = TRUE)

# First two lines viewing RCC as text file

# FileVersion,1.7 SoftwareVersion,6.0.2
# ID,01 Owner, Comments, Date,20260408 GeneRLF,NS_Mm_IO_360_v1.0 SystemAPF,n6_vDV1 ID,12 FovCount,280 FovCounted,280 ScannerID,2212E0093 StagePosition,1 BindingDensity,1.46 CartridgeID,day 10 CartridgeBarcode, 
```

Run with default nSolver normalization to get the QC metrics. 
You can change the normalization method later, but you need to run this first to get the QC metrics.

```{r}
dat <- processNanostringData(
                  nsFiles = rcc_files, 
                  normalization='nSolver',
                  output.format = "list", 
                  includeQC = TRUE)
```


# QC

```{r}
# Positive control
posQC <- positiveQC(dat)$tab %>%
   clean_names() %>%
   remove_rownames()

posQC_plt <- positiveQC(dat)$plt

# Negative control
negQC <- negativeQC(dat, interactive.plot = FALSE)$tab %>%
   clean_names() %>%
   rownames_to_column("sample") %>%
   mutate(genes_below_bg_count = as.integer(sub(" \\(.*\\)", "", genes_below_bg_percent)),
          genes_below_bg_percent = as.numeric(sub(".*\\((.*)%\\)", "\\1", genes_below_bg_percent)))

negQC_plt <- negativeQC(dat)$plt

# Housekeeping normalization scale factors
hkQC <- data.frame(hk_scale_factor = dat$hk.scalefactors) %>% 
      rownames_to_column("sample")
```

```{r}
# Add QC from the RCC file and join with the other QC metrics and metadata
qc_data_sample <- data.frame(dat$qc) %>% 
   rownames_to_column(var = "sample") %>%
   mutate() %>%
   left_join(posQC, by = "sample") %>%
   left_join(negQC, by = "sample") %>%
   left_join(hkQC, by = "sample") %>%
   clean_names() %>%
   mutate(binding_density = as.numeric(binding_density),
          fov_counted = as.numeric(fov_counted),
          fov_count = as.numeric(fov_count),
          pct_fov_counted = fov_counted / fov_count * 100)

qc_data_sample$pct_features_nonzero <- apply(X = dat$exprs.raw, MARGIN = 2, function(x) sum(x > 0)/nrow(dat$exprs.raw) * 100)
```

## FOV

At least 75% of FOVs should be successfully counted to obtain robust data.

```{r}
qc_data_sample %>%
   ggplot(aes(y = sample, x = pct_fov_counted)) +
   geom_col() +
   xlab("% FOV counted") +
   ylab("Sample name") +
   geom_vline(xintercept = 75, color = "red", linewidth = 1) +
   theme_bw(base_size = 12)
```

Sample "day 14_01_06" fails.

## Nonzero Features

```{r}
qc_data_sample %>%
   ggplot(aes(y = sample, x = pct_features_nonzero)) +
   geom_col() +
   xlab("% nonzero features") +
   ylab("Sample name") +
   theme_bw(base_size = 12)
```

Sample "day 14_01_06" has slightly less.

## Features below negative control

```{r}
qc_data_sample %>%
   filter(mean_neg > 0) %>%
   ggplot(aes(y = sample, x = genes_below_bg_percent)) +
   geom_col() +
   xlab("% genes below negative control background") +
   ylab("Sample name") +
   theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
   ggtitle("", subtitle = "Only samples with mean negative control counts above 0 are included in this plot")
```

May of the "day 10" samples have significantly more genes below background, many over 50-75%.

## Binding Density

The ideal range 0.1 - 2.25 spots per square micron has been established for assays run on an nCounter MAX or FLEX system 
and 0.1 - 1.8 spots per square micron on the nCounter SPRINT system. 

The Nanostring FAS suggested this is actually a conservative cutoff and so long as the binding density is similar among 
samples, a lower binding density may provide usable data.

```{r}
qc_data_sample %>%
   ggplot(aes(y = sample, x = binding_density)) +
   geom_col() +
   xlab("Binding Density") +
   ylab("Sample name") +
   geom_vline(xintercept = 0.1, color = "blue", linewidth = 1) +
   geom_vline(xintercept = 1.8, color = "blue", linewidth = 1) +
   theme_bw(base_size = 12)
```

Sample "day 14_01_06" fails, much too high.

## Positive control linearity

This metric performs a correlation analysis in log2 space between the known concentrations of positive control 
target molecules added by NanoString and the resulting counts. Correlation values lower than 0.95 may indicate 
an issue with the hybridization reaction and/or assay performance.

```{r}
qc_data_sample %>%
   ggplot(aes(y = sample, x = r_squared)) +
   geom_col() +
   xlab("Correlation value of positive control") +
   ylab("Sample name") +
   geom_vline(xintercept = 0.95, color = "red", size = 1) +
   theme_bw(base_size = 12)
```

Sample "day 14_01_06" has no data (probably no control detection).

```{r}
posQC_plt
```


## POS A

```{r poscontrol}
# Extract positive control counts
positive_control_names <- data.frame(dat$dict) %>%
   filter(CodeClass == "Positive") %>% pull(Accession)
positive_control_counts <- dat$exprs[positive_control_names, ]
positive_control_counts <- data.frame(positive_control_counts) %>% 
   tibble::rownames_to_column(var = "Accession") %>%
   left_join(data.frame(dat$dict), by = "Accession") %>%
   relocate(Name) %>% select(-CodeClass)
positive_control_counts %<>% pivot_longer(-c(Name, Accession), names_to = "sample", values_to = "count")
```

The Nanostring FAS noted that POS A should be above about 10K counts. The concern is that positive control 
normalization when Pos A is lower than this could amplify noise instead of reducing it. This flag would 
probably co-occur with LOD or linearity flags.  

```{r}
positive_control_counts %>%
   filter(Name == "POS_A(128)") %>%
   ggplot(aes(y = sample, x = count)) +
   geom_col() +
   xlab("Counts of POS_A") +
   ylab("Sample name") +
   theme_bw(base_size = 12)
```

Sample "day 14_01_06" fails.

## Negative control background

```{r}
negQC_plt
```

Everything is below 30.

## Positive control LOD

This measures the limit of detection of the assay by comparing the results from the positive control 
probes and those from the negative control probes. Specifically, it is expected that the 0.5 fM positive 
control probe (Pos_E) will produce raw counts at least two standard deviations higher than the mean of 
the negative control probes.

```{r negcontrol}
# Extract control counts
negative_control_names <- data.frame(dat$dict) %>%
   filter(CodeClass == "Negative") %>% pull(Accession)
negative_control_counts <- dat$exprs[negative_control_names, ]
negative_control_counts <- data.frame(negative_control_counts) %>% 
   tibble::rownames_to_column(var = "Accession") %>%
   left_join(data.frame(dat$dict), by = "Accession") %>%
   relocate(Name) %>% select(-CodeClass)
negative_control_counts %<>% pivot_longer(-c(Name, Accession), names_to = "sample", values_to = "count")

controls_df <- positive_control_counts %>% 
   filter(Name == "POS_E(0.5)") %>% 
   select(sample, pos_E = count) %>%
   left_join(negative_control_counts %>% 
               group_by(sample) %>% 
               summarize(negative_control_mean = mean(count), 
                         negative_control_sd = sd(count)), by = "sample") %>%
   mutate(positive_control_lod = (pos_E - negative_control_mean)/negative_control_sd) %>% 
   left_join(positive_control_counts %>% 
   filter(Name == "POS_A(128)") %>% 
   select(sample, pos_A = count), by = "sample")

# Samples are in same order although names slightly different
qc_data_sample <- bind_cols(qc_data_sample, controls_df %>% select(-sample))
```

```{r}
positive_control_counts %>%
   ggplot(aes(y = sample, x = count)) +
   geom_jitter(shape = 21, fill = "gray", width=0, height=0.1) +
   xlab("Counts of positive controls") +
   ylab("Sample name") +
   theme_bw(base_size = 12)
```

Sample "day 14_01_06" has much lower counts than the rest of the samples, which seem consistent in magnitude.
"day 10" samples have slightly higher values of the highest postitive control compared to "day 14" samples.

```{r}
bind_rows(negative_control_counts %>% mutate(ControlType = "negative"), positive_control_counts %>% mutate(ControlType = "positive")) %>%
   ggplot(aes(y = sample, x = count, fill = ControlType)) +
   geom_jitter(shape = 21, width=0, height=0.2, alpha = 0.5) +
   xlab("Counts of positive and negative controls") +
   ylab("Sample name") +
   theme_bw(base_size = 12)
```

Sample "day 14_01_06" has low positive, mixed in with negative.

```{r}
controls_df %>%
   ggplot(aes(y = sample)) +
   geom_point(aes(x = negative_control_mean), color = "blue") +
   geom_point(aes(x = pos_E), color = "red") +
   geom_errorbar(aes(x = negative_control_mean, xmin = negative_control_mean, xmax = negative_control_mean + negative_control_sd*2)) +
   ylab("") + xlab("Count") + ggtitle("Mean of negative controls + 2 stdev of negative\ncontrols < POS_E")
```

Sample "day 14_01_06" fails and should definitely be removed.

```{r}
controls_df %>%
   ggplot(aes(y = sample, x = positive_control_lod)) +
   geom_col() +
   xlab("Number of negative-control standard deviations\nabove the negative-control mean of POS_E") +
   ylab("Sample name") +
   geom_vline(xintercept = 2, color = "red", size = 1) +
   theme_bw(base_size = 12)
```
